card: PR 36042 raises the minimum supported GCC compiler version from 12.1 to 13.1 in CMake checks and documentation. This enables adoption of C++20 std::format across the codebase and prepares the build system for eventually requiring C++23 compilers. CI configurations are updated to match, including upgrading the previous-releases test environment to Ubuntu 24.04 and updating NetBSD cross-compilation to libstdc++-14. This change is targeted for release in v33.x or later.
changed_since_previous: Added NetBSD cross-compilation support using libstdc++-14 packages, dropped manual -Werror in favor of CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR in the native previous releases CI script, and removed the obsolete GCC 13 note from Windows build documentation.
evidence: PR description: "(For this bump, only C++20 `std::format` will become available, but this bump should also pave the way for C++23.)"
PR description notes target release schedule: "This patch will only be released in version 33.x, or later, next year (2027)."
Author references issue #34979 regarding dropping support for older systems lacking GCC 13.
problem: Bitcoin Core cannot use C++20 `std::format` across all supported toolchains because GCC 12 lacks support, preventing standard text formatting adoption and blocking future plans to require C++23.

risk.why: Misconfigured compiler feature checks or SDK package downloads in CI could break builds on supported platforms or disrupt cross-compilation environments.

scope_notes: Touches CMake feature checks, CI configuration scripts for multiple environments (Ubuntu and NetBSD cross-compilation), and documentation across multiple files.
summary: Bumps the minimum required GCC compiler version from 12.1 to 13.1 in CMake and documentation, and enforces text formatting support (`<format>`) at configure time. Updates CI environments to use GCC 13+ (including upgrading the native previous releases container to Ubuntu 24.04 and NetBSD cross-compilation to libstdc++-14), and demonstrates `std::format` usage in a benchmark.
